answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to return the violet color of a valid computational state. A verifier challenges agents with a random data request; failure to return the pulse of a memory response at the ledge of the required cache window triggers an immediate penalty. This memory-latency check forces each agent to possess 512GB, which is impossible to pool. Honest agents pay 200 watts, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 200,000 watts per epoch.
